answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can work like a walled garden: entry requires a refundable stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, so each fake identity costs real money. Reputation then accrues slowly — a newcomer starts on a narrow ledge with limited privileges and only climbs as its work is attested by independent peers. The mirror is public audit: every attestation and stake is visible on-ledger, so a cluster of sock-puppet agents endorsing each other stands out as a closed loop, and reviewers can discount or slash the whole ring at once.
